title: shrinking the window while a completion listing is displayed blanks zshrs's screen — zsh keeps all 3 non-blank rows at 24x80 -> 14x80, zshrs keeps 0

observed.detail: zsh kept 3 non-blank row(s), zshrs kept 0
observed.notes: Both shells reach the resize with the SAME 3 non-blank rows on screen (the replayer records `n_before` for each side), so this is not a completion difference showing up late — the listing is there, and the resize is what removes it. Direction matters and is pinned as controls: GROWING the window 24->30 keeps 3 rows on both shells, and setting the window to the size it already has keeps 3 on both. Shrinking is the only move that loses anything, and it is not a threshold effect: one row smaller (24->23) already costs zshrs a row (zsh 3, zshrs 2 — variant0), and shrinking the width too (24x80 -> 14x60) leaves zsh with 4 rows and zshrs with 0 (variant1). Cells at `zsh -f` defaults: no compsys, no zstyle, TAB is expand-or-complete.

controls.note: the same completion, window GROWN 24->30. PASS (3 rows on both) — the direction of the resize is the variable
the same completion, window set to the size it already has. PASS (3 rows on both) — receiving a SIGWINCH is not itself the trigger

variants.note: one row smaller. zsh 3, zshrs 2 — the loss is proportional, not a cliff at some minimum height
narrower as well as shorter. zsh 4 (it re-lays the listing out), zshrs 0

origin: reported in round 5 as a shrinking SIGWINCH blanking zshrs's screen while a listing is displayed, with grows and same-size resizes fine
re-run first-hand in round 6; the one-row and narrower-too measurements were taken here

zshrs_binary.kind: debug build under target/ (NOT the Homebrew-installed zshrs)

zsh_binary.note: Homebrew zsh 5.9.2, which is what `zsh` on PATH resolves to here; /bin/zsh is an older build and is NOT what any harness runs.

confirmed.note: round 6. Reproduced FIRST-HAND, then pinned through tests/compsys_fixtures/winch_probe.py, which was written for this finding: no sibling harness changes the window size mid-cell.
